questions.q: For pure ALOHA with frame time T, the vulnerable time of a frame is:
questions.exp: A frame can collide with any frame sent in the interval T before or T after it, so vulnerable time is 2T.

questions.q: Which of the following is the IPv4 loopback address?
questions.exp: The 127.0.0.0/8 block is reserved for loopback; 127.0.0.1 is the standard address.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs consists only of lossy compression formats?
questions.exp: JPEG (images) and MP3 (audio) discard information. PNG, ZIP, GIF, FLAC, Huffman and RLE are lossless.

questions.q: Four sources of 16 kbps each are multiplexed by synchronous TDM with one bit per slot. What is the duration of one frame?
questions.exp: Each source produces one bit every 1/16000 s = 62.5 µs, so a frame (one bit from each source) must last 62.5 µs.

questions.q: DHCP servers listen for client requests using which transport protocol and port?
questions.exp: DHCP uses UDP; the server uses port 67 and the client uses port 68.

questions.q: What is the default port number of HTTPS?
questions.exp: HTTPS uses TCP port 443 by default; HTTP uses 80.

questions.q: A network has addresses 192.168.0.0/24 and 192.168.1.0/24. Which single prefix summarises both?
questions.exp: The two blocks differ only in the 24th bit, so combining them gives 192.168.0.0/23.

questions.q: Light is confined inside an optical fibre core mainly because of:
questions.exp: The core has a higher refractive index than the cladding, so light is guided by total internal reflection.

questions.q: A file of 50 MB (1 MB = 10⁶ bytes) is sent over a 100 Mbps link at full speed, ignoring overheads. How long does it take?
questions.exp: Size = 50 × 10⁶ × 8 = 400 × 10⁶ bits; time = 400 Mb / 100 Mbps = 4 s.

questions.q: What is the minimum length of a TCP header (without options)?
questions.exp: The TCP header has 20 bytes of mandatory fields; options can extend it up to 60 bytes.

questions.q: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets from source host to destination host across networks?
questions.exp: The network layer handles logical addressing and routing of packets between networks.

questions.q: A link has a bandwidth of 100 Mbps and a round-trip time of 40 ms. What is its bandwidth-delay product?
A line reduces the power of a signal from 100 mW to 1 mW. What is the attenuation?
questions.exp: dB loss = 10 log10(P1/P2) = 10 log10(100) = 20 dB.

questions.q:
Statement I: In CSMA/CD a station keeps listening to the channel while it is transmitting.
Statement II: After a collision, Ethernet stations wait for a random time chosen by binary exponential backoff.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true
questions.exp: CSMA/CD detects collisions by monitoring the medium during transmission and uses binary exponential backoff for retransmission.

questions.q: A 2D even-parity scheme is used on a 4 × 4 block. The receiver finds that the parity of row 2 and of column 3 is wrong. Which data bit is in error?
questions.exp: The single bad bit lies at the intersection of the failing row (2) and failing column (3).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true about UDP?
options: It provides in-order delivery of datagrams
It supports an optional checksum for error detection
questions.exp: UDP does not guarantee ordering or delivery; those are TCP features.

questions.q: How many cable links are needed to connect 12 PCs in a star network through a central switch?
questions.exp: Each PC has one link to the switch, so 12 links are needed.

questions.q: In an ARP request, the destination MAC address in the Ethernet frame is
options: the MAC address of the default gateway
the MAC address of the target host, already known
questions.exp: The sender does not yet know the target MAC, so the request is broadcast to the whole LAN; only the owner of the IP replies, by unicast.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the split horizon technique in distance vector routing?
options: To increase bandwidth for routing updates
To prevent routing loops by not advertising a route back out of the interface it was learned from
questions.exp: Split horizon avoids advertising a route to the neighbour from which it was learned, reducing count-to-infinity loops.

questions.q: How many segments are normally exchanged to terminate a TCP connection gracefully?
questions.exp: Each direction is closed separately with a FIN and an ACK, giving four segments.

questions.q: Which statement about SMTP is correct?
options: It is a pull protocol used by users to read mail from the mailbox
It keeps messages on the server and synchronises folders
It is a push protocol used to send and relay mail between servers over TCP port 25
questions.exp: SMTP pushes mail from client to server and server to server. Retrieval is done by POP3 or IMAP.

questions.q: What is the minimum size of an Ethernet frame (IEEE 802.3), including header and CRC?
questions.exp: Minimum Ethernet frame is 64 bytes (46 bytes minimum data plus 18 bytes of header and FCS).

questions.q: In active-mode FTP, which port does the server use for the data connection?
questions.exp: FTP uses port 21 for control and port 20 for data in active mode.

questions.q: A message of 6000 bits is sent over a path of 3 links, each 1 Mbps, with negligible propagation delay. It is split into six packets of 1000 bits using store-and-forward packet switching. What is the total time to deliver it?
questions.exp: Each packet takes 1 ms per link. Total = (packets + links − 1) × 1 ms = (6 + 3 − 1) = 8 ms.

questions.q: Data bits 1101011 are to be sent using even parity. What should the parity bit be?
questions.exp: The data has five 1s (odd), so a parity bit of 1 makes the total number of 1s even.

questions.q: Which device performs modulation and demodulation of signals?
questions.exp: A modem converts digital data to analog signals for transmission over telephone or cable lines and back again.

questions.q: Which device regenerates and retransmits a weakened signal at the physical layer?
questions.exp: A repeater works at the physical layer and amplifies/regenerates signals to extend the cable length.

questions.q: Using the CRC generator polynomial x³ + x + 1 (1011), what is the CRC to be appended to data 1101?
questions.exp: Dividing 1101000 by 1011 (mod-2) leaves remainder 001, so the transmitted word is 1101001.

questions.q: In which switching technique are the packets of one message routed independently and may arrive out of order?
questions.exp: In datagram switching each packet is routed independently, so packets can take different paths and arrive out of order.

questions.q: A noiseless channel has a bandwidth of 4 kHz and uses 8 signal levels. What is the maximum bit rate by Nyquist's theorem?
A 7-bit Hamming code (even parity, parity bits at positions 1, 2 and 4) is received as 0110001. Which bit position is in error?

Match the OSI layer with its function.
P. Physical  Q. Data link  R. Network  S. Transport
1. Process-to-process delivery  2. Hop-to-hop frame delivery using MAC addresses  3. Host-to-host routing  4. Transmission of raw bits
questions.exp: Physical sends bits, data link delivers frames hop to hop, network routes host to host and transport gives process-to-process delivery.

questions.q: How many point-to-point links are required to connect 8 nodes in a fully connected mesh topology?
Which HTTP status code indicates that the requested resource was not found?
questions.exp: 404 means Not Found; 403 is Forbidden, 500 is Internal Server Error and 301 is Moved Permanently.

questions.q: A Go-Back-N sender transmits frames 0 to 7. Frame 3 is lost but frames 4 to 7 reach the receiver. After the timeout, how many frames are retransmitted?
questions.exp: Go-Back-N resends the lost frame and all that followed it: frames 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 = 5 frames.

questions.q: Which layer of the TCP/IP model corresponds to the network layer of the OSI model?
questions.exp: The Internet layer (IP) of TCP/IP corresponds to the OSI network layer.

questions.q: In passive-mode FTP, which side initiates the data connection?
questions.exp: In passive mode the server opens a port and the client connects to it, which works through client-side firewalls and NAT. In active mode the server connects back from port 20.

questions.q:
Statement I: OSPF routers flood link-state advertisements to build a view of the topology.
Statement II: RIP uses link bandwidth as its routing metric.
options: Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true
questions.exp: OSPF is link-state with flooding; RIP uses hop count, not bandwidth, as its metric.

questions.q: A TCP sender in slow start begins with cwnd = 1 MSS and receives all acknowledgements correctly, with ssthresh very large. What is cwnd after four successful round trips?
questions.exp: In slow start cwnd doubles every RTT: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16.

questions.q: What does a persistent connection in HTTP/1.1 mean?
options: The server remembers the client identity using cookies
The connection is encrypted with TLS
Several requests and responses are sent over the same TCP connection
Every object needs a new TCP connection
questions.exp: HTTP/1.0 opened one TCP connection per object; HTTP/1.1 keeps the connection open by default, saving handshakes.

questions.q: What is the maximum channel utilization (throughput) of pure ALOHA?
questions.exp: Pure ALOHA maximum throughput is 1/(2e) ≈ 0.184, i.e. 18.4%.

questions.q: Which transmission medium is immune to electromagnetic interference?
questions.exp: Optical fibre carries light, not electrical signals, so it is not affected by EMI.

questions.q: What is meant by piggybacking in the data link layer?
options: Combining several small packets into one
Attaching the acknowledgement to an outgoing data frame
questions.exp: In piggybacking, the ACK for received data is carried in the header of the next data frame going the other way.

questions.q: What is the length of the preamble (excluding the start frame delimiter) in a classic Ethernet frame?
questions.exp: The preamble is 7 bytes of alternating 1010... followed by a 1-byte SFD.

questions.q: Eight PCs are each connected to a different port of an 8-port switch. How many collision domains exist?
questions.exp: Each switch port is its own collision domain, so there are 8 (while there is just one broadcast domain).

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Wireless LANs use CSMA/CA instead of CSMA/CD.
Reason (R): A wireless station cannot reliably detect collisions while it is transmitting.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Transmit and receive power levels differ greatly, so collision detection is impractical; hence collision avoidance is used.

questions.q: Which e-mail retrieval protocol keeps messages on the server and synchronises mailbox folders across several devices?
questions.exp: IMAP leaves mail on the server and maintains mailbox state for multiple clients; SMTP only sends mail.

questions.q: After the third consecutive collision in Ethernet, a station chooses a random wait multiplier K from:
questions.exp: After the nth collision K is chosen from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1; for n = 3 this is 0 to 7.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of hops a valid route can have in RIP?
questions.exp: RIP treats a metric of 16 as infinity, so the maximum valid hop count is 15.

questions.q: Which of the following addresses can be assigned to a host in the subnet 192.168.4.64/27?
questions.exp: The /27 block is 64–95; 64 is the network address and 95 is broadcast, so 94 is the last usable host address.

questions.q:
Match the protocol with its default port.
P. SMTP  Q. POP3  R. FTP (control)  S. DNS
1. 110  2. 21  3. 53  4. 25
questions.exp: SMTP uses 25, POP3 uses 110, FTP control uses 21 and DNS uses 53.

questions.q: An organisation has 192.168.5.0/24 and needs at least 6 equal-sized subnets. What is the maximum number of usable hosts in each subnet?
questions.exp: Six subnets need 3 borrowed bits (8 subnets), leaving 5 host bits: 2⁵ − 2 = 30.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a field in the UDP header?
questions.exp: The UDP header has source port, destination port, length and checksum; it has no sequence number.

questions.q: A host has the address 172.16.37.200/20. What is its network address?
questions.exp: /20 gives mask 255.255.240.0. Third octet 37 = 00100101; ANDing with 11110000 gives 00100000 = 32, so the network is 172.16.32.0.

questions.q: A Selective Repeat protocol uses 4-bit sequence numbers. What is the maximum window size?
questions.exp: For Selective Repeat, the maximum window is 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 2³ = 8.

questions.q: What is the maximum payload (MTU) of a standard Ethernet frame?
questions.exp: Standard Ethernet allows up to 1500 bytes of payload; the full frame with header and FCS is 1518 bytes.

questions.q: An IPv4 datagram of total length 4000 bytes (20-byte header) is sent over a link with MTU 1500 bytes. What is the fragment offset field value of the third fragment?
questions.exp: Each fragment carries 1480 data bytes (offset unit 8 bytes). Third fragment starts at 2960 bytes, so offset = 2960/8 = 370.

questions.q: The Protocol Data Unit (PDU) at the data link layer is called a:
questions.exp: Data link layer PDUs are frames; transport has segments, network has packets, physical has bits.

questions.q: How many addresses are there in the CIDR block 10.0.0.0/8?
questions.exp: A /8 leaves 24 host bits: 2²⁴ = 16,777,216 addresses.

questions.q: ARP is used to map:
options: a MAC address to an IP address
a domain name to an IP address
a port number to an IP address
an IP address to a MAC address
questions.exp: The Address Resolution Protocol finds the MAC address that corresponds to a known IP address on the local network.

questions.q: What is the correct order of messages in DHCP address assignment?
questions.exp: The DORA sequence is Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

questions.q: In slotted ALOHA with an offered load G = 1 frame per slot, the throughput S = G·e^(−G) is approximately:
questions.exp: S = 1 × e⁻¹ ≈ 0.368, which is also the maximum throughput of slotted ALOHA.

questions.q:
Match the generation with its technology.
P. 1G  Q. 2G  R. 3G  S. 4G
1. LTE  2. AMPS (analog)  3. GSM  4. WCDMA/UMTS
questions.exp: 1G used analog AMPS, 2G used GSM, 3G used UMTS/WCDMA and 4G uses LTE.

questions.q: A TCP sender sends a segment starting at sequence number 4000 and carrying 600 bytes of data. What acknowledgement number will the receiver return when it is received correctly?
questions.exp: The ACK number is the next byte expected: 4000 + 600 = 4600.

questions.q: In a network, the link costs are A–B = 4, A–C = 2, C–B = 1, B–D = 5, C–D = 8 and D–E = 3. What is the shortest-path cost from A to E?
Which of the following is a lossless data compression technique?
questions.exp: Huffman coding (like RLE and LZW) lets the original data be recovered exactly. JPEG, MP3 and MPEG discard information and are lossy.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of segments in the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.exp: The client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client completes with ACK.

questions.q: Which traffic-shaping technique sends packets into the network at a constant rate irrespective of how bursty the arrival is?
questions.exp: Leaky bucket outputs at a fixed rate; extra packets wait in the bucket or are discarded. Token bucket, by contrast, permits bursts.

questions.q: According to the Nyquist sampling theorem, the minimum sampling rate needed to digitise a signal whose highest frequency is 5 kHz is
questions.exp: The sampling rate must be at least twice the highest frequency: 2 x 5 kHz = 10 kHz.

questions.q: Which of the following is a link-state routing protocol?
questions.exp: OSPF floods link-state advertisements and runs Dijkstra's algorithm; RIP and IGRP are distance vector and BGP is path vector.

questions.q: A Go-Back-N protocol uses 3-bit sequence numbers. What is the maximum sender window size?
questions.exp: For Go-Back-N the maximum window is 2ⁿ − 1 = 2³ − 1 = 7.

questions.q: Which kind of noise is caused by the random motion of electrons in a conductor and cannot be eliminated?
questions.exp: Thermal noise exists in all conductors above absolute zero. Crosstalk is coupling between wires, impulse noise is a short spike, induced noise comes from motors and appliances.

questions.q: Run-length encoding of the string AAAABBBCCD gives
questions.exp: Runs: AAAA (4A), BBB (3B), CC (2C), D (1D).

questions.q: Why is UDP preferred over TCP for real-time voice calls?
options: It guarantees delivery of every packet
It avoids connection set-up and retransmission delays that harm real-time flow
questions.exp: Real-time voice tolerates some loss but not delay, so UDP's low overhead and no retransmission suit it.

questions.q: Silly window syndrome is a problem related to:
options: Flow control with very small window advertisements
questions.exp: It arises when sender or receiver exchanges tiny segments because of small window updates, wasting bandwidth.

questions.q: In a star topology with a central hub, the failure of which component brings down the entire network?
questions.exp: All traffic passes through the hub, so hub failure is a single point of failure for the whole network.

questions.q: Which device can interconnect networks that use different protocols and architectures?
questions.exp: A gateway performs protocol conversion and can connect dissimilar networks.

questions.q: How many parity (check) bits are needed in a Hamming code to protect 11 data bits against single-bit errors?
questions.exp: Need 2ʳ ≥ m + r + 1. For r = 3: 8 ≥ 15 fails; for r = 4: 16 ≥ 16 holds. So r = 4.

questions.q: Which port number is used by the SSH protocol?
questions.exp: SSH uses TCP port 22; 21 is FTP, 23 Telnet and 25 SMTP.

questions.q: Which of the following is a private IPv4 address?
Which DNS record type maps a host name to an IPv4 address?
questions.exp: The A record holds the IPv4 address of a host; AAAA holds IPv6.

questions.q: Attenuation of a signal over a long cable is overcome by using
options: twisting the wires of the cable
questions.exp: Attenuation is loss of signal strength with distance; amplifiers or repeaters regenerate it. Twisting and shielding reduce crosstalk, and CRC detects errors only.

questions.q: In an SMTP session, which command specifies the recipient of the message?
questions.exp: SMTP dialogue: HELO/EHLO, MAIL FROM (sender), RCPT TO (recipient), DATA (body ending with a dot line), QUIT.

questions.q: A TCP sender has cwnd = 32 MSS when a timeout occurs. What is the new value of ssthresh?
questions.exp: On timeout ssthresh is set to half of the current cwnd, 32/2 = 16 MSS, and cwnd restarts from 1 MSS.

questions.q: In a stop-and-wait protocol, a link has 1 Mbps bandwidth, frames of 1000 bits and one-way propagation delay of 4 ms. What is the link utilization?
questions.exp: Tt = 1 ms, Tp = 4 ms. Utilization = Tt/(Tt + 2Tp) = 1/9 ≈ 11.1%.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an application layer protocol?
questions.exp: ICMP works at the network (Internet) layer; HTTP, DNS and SMTP are application layer protocols.

questions.q: Which interframe space is the shortest in IEEE 802.11 DCF operation?
questions.exp: SIFS is the shortest, giving highest priority to ACK, CTS and similar frames; the order is SIFS < PIFS < DIFS < EIFS.

questions.q: Data 10110 is to be sent using the CRC generator 1001 (x³ + 1). What CRC bits are appended?
questions.exp: Dividing 10110000 by 1001 (mod-2) leaves remainder 100.

questions.q: A CRC with a generator polynomial of degree 16 guarantees detection of all burst errors of length at most:
questions.exp: A CRC with r check bits detects every burst error of length ≤ r, here 16.

questions.q: Which DNS server provides the final, authoritative mapping for the host names of a domain?
questions.exp: The authoritative name server of a domain stores its actual resource records; root and TLD servers only refer queries onward.

questions.q: One million bits are sent over a 2 Mbps link with a propagation delay of 20 ms. Ignoring other delays, how long until the last bit arrives?
questions.exp: Transmission time = 10⁶ / 2×10⁶ = 0.5 s = 500 ms; adding 20 ms propagation gives 520 ms.

questions.q: Which IPv6 address prefix identifies link-local unicast addresses?
questions.exp: Link-local addresses begin with FE80::/10; global unicast starts 2000::/3, multicast FF00::/8 and unique local FC00::/7.

questions.q: In the Go-Back-N protocol the receiver window size is:
questions.exp: A Go-Back-N receiver accepts only the next in-order frame, so its window size is 1.

questions.q: A 1500-byte packet is sent over a 10 Mbps link. What is the transmission delay?
questions.exp: Transmission delay = 1500 × 8 bits / 10⁷ bps = 12000 / 10⁷ = 1.2 ms.

questions.q: Which field of the TCP header is used by the receiver to implement flow control?
questions.exp: The receiver advertises its available buffer space through the window size field.

questions.q: A block code has a minimum Hamming distance of 5. How many errors can it correct?
questions.exp: Correctable errors = ⌊(dmin − 1)/2⌋ = 2 (it can detect up to 4).

questions.q: Which field of the IPv4 header has been removed in the IPv6 header?
questions.exp: IPv6 drops the header checksum to speed up router processing; TTL became Hop Limit.

questions.q: In a 10 Mbps CSMA/CD LAN the one-way propagation delay between the two farthest stations is 25.6 µs. What is the minimum frame size needed to detect collisions?
questions.exp: Frame transmission time must be ≥ 2Tp = 51.2 µs, so size = 51.2 µs × 10⁷ bps = 512 bits (64 bytes).

questions.q: Two 8-bit words 10110011 and 01101100 are added using one's complement arithmetic and the sum is complemented to form the checksum. What is the checksum?
questions.exp: 179 + 108 = 287 = 1 0001 1111; wrapping the carry gives 00100000; its complement is 11011111.

questions.q: A QPSK modem signals at 2400 baud. What is its bit rate?
questions.exp: QPSK has 4 phases = 2 bits per signal element: 2400 x 2 = 4800 bps.

questions.q: ARP messages are carried directly in
questions.exp: ARP is encapsulated straight in an Ethernet frame (EtherType 0x0806) and is not routed beyond the local network.

questions.q: A noisy channel of 3000 Hz bandwidth has a signal-to-noise ratio of 1023 (linear). What is the Shannon capacity?
Which set of 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi channels (20 MHz wide) are non-overlapping?
questions.exp: Channels 1, 6 and 11 are spaced at least 25 MHz apart and do not overlap.

questions.q: Which TCP flag is used to abruptly abort or reset a connection?
questions.exp: The RST flag immediately resets the connection, unlike FIN which closes it gracefully.

questions.q: The IP address 172.20.5.9 belongs to which class?
questions.exp: Class B addresses have first octet in the range 128–191; 172 lies in this range.

questions.q: How many hexadecimal digits are there in a full IPv6 address (ignoring colons)?
questions.exp: 128 bits / 4 bits per hex digit = 32 hexadecimal digits.

questions.q: In NRZ-I encoding, a bit 1 is represented by
options: a transition in the middle of the bit only
a change (transition) of signal level at the beginning of the bit
questions.exp: NRZ-I (inverted) toggles the level for every 1 and keeps it for 0, so long runs of 0s can still lose synchronisation.

questions.q: Which multiplexing technique combines several optical signals of different wavelengths onto a single optical fibre?
questions.exp: Wavelength Division Multiplexing assigns each signal its own light wavelength on the same fibre.

questions.q: Which technique assigns time slots dynamically only to those inputs that have data to send?
questions.exp: Statistical TDM allocates slots on demand, so no capacity is wasted on idle inputs.

questions.q: Router X is 2 hops-cost away from neighbour Y. Y advertises a distance of 5 to network Z. X currently has a distance of 9 to Z. After applying the distance vector update, what is X's distance to Z?
questions.exp: New cost via Y = 2 + 5 = 7, which is less than 9, so X updates to 7.

questions.q: In Manchester encoding, every bit period contains
options: a transition only when the bit is 1
a transition only at the end of a 0 bit
a transition in the middle of the bit, which also provides clock synchronisation
no transition at all; the level stays constant
questions.exp: Manchester (IEEE 802.3) is self-clocking: each bit has a mid-bit transition, and its direction gives the bit value. The price is double bandwidth.

questions.q: Which network device forwards frames to a specific port by learning MAC addresses?
questions.exp: A layer-2 switch maintains a MAC address table and forwards frames only to the port of the destination.

questions.q: Which technique allows many hosts with private addresses to share a single public IPv4 address?
questions.exp: Network Address Translation rewrites private addresses (and ports) to a public address at the border router.

questions.q: A token bucket differs from a leaky bucket in that the token bucket
options: always outputs at a constant rate
drops every packet that arrives in a burst
allows bursts, by saving tokens during idle periods up to the bucket size
questions.exp: Idle time accumulates tokens, so a burst up to the bucket capacity can be sent at full speed; a leaky bucket never exceeds its fixed output rate.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct shortened form of the IPv6 address 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329?
questions.exp: Leading zeros are dropped and one run of all-zero groups is replaced by '::', giving 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329.

questions.q: How does an Ethernet switch learn which stations are reachable through which port?
options: By examining the destination IP of frames
By examining the source MAC address of incoming frames
questions.exp: A learning switch records the source MAC address and arrival port of each frame in its forwarding table.

questions.q: Which switching technique reserves a dedicated end-to-end path for the whole duration of the communication?
questions.exp: Circuit switching sets up and holds a dedicated path between the two endpoints until the call ends.

questions.q: An IPv4 header carries no options. What value does its HLEN field contain?
questions.exp: HLEN counts 4-byte words; the 20-byte base header gives 20/4 = 5.

questions.q: Which problem is typically associated with distance vector routing protocols?
questions.exp: Slow propagation of bad news in distance vector protocols causes the count-to-infinity problem.

questions.q: HDLC bit stuffing is applied to the data 0111111 (flag = 01111110). What is transmitted?
questions.exp: After five consecutive 1s the sender inserts a 0: 0 11111 [0] 1 = 01111101, so the data can never imitate the flag.

questions.q: A voice signal of bandwidth 4 kHz is digitised by PCM at the Nyquist sampling rate with 8 bits per sample. What is the bit rate?
questions.exp: Nyquist rate = 2 x 4 kHz = 8000 samples/s; 8000 x 8 bits = 64,000 bps.

questions.q: A class B network with mask 255.255.252.0 is used. How many usable hosts does each subnet have?
questions.exp: Mask 255.255.252.0 is /22, leaving 10 host bits: 2¹⁰ − 2 = 1022.

questions.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for dialog control and synchronization using checkpoints?
questions.exp: The session layer manages dialogs and inserts synchronization points (checkpoints) in a data stream.

questions.q: Which topology uses a single backbone cable terminated at both ends to which all nodes are connected?
questions.exp: A bus topology uses one shared backbone cable with terminators at each end.

questions.q: Which OSI layer is concerned with data encryption, compression and translation of data formats?
questions.exp: The presentation layer handles syntax, translation, encryption and compression.

questions.q: In IEEE 802.11 infrastructure mode, one access point together with its associated stations forms a:
questions.exp: An AP and its associated stations constitute a BSS; several BSSs joined by a distribution system form an ESS.

questions.q: Which protocol provides the security layer used by HTTPS?
questions.exp: HTTPS is HTTP carried over TLS (formerly SSL), providing encryption and authentication.

questions.q: A single parity bit can detect:
options: Any odd number of bit errors
Any even number of bit errors
questions.exp: Any odd number of flipped bits changes the parity, but even numbers of flips cancel out and go undetected.

questions.q: How many usable host addresses are available in the network 192.168.10.0/28?
questions.exp: /28 leaves 4 host bits: 2⁴ − 2 = 14 usable hosts.

questions.q: A router sends a choke packet to a source host when
options: it detects congestion and wants the source to reduce its sending rate
the TTL of a packet reaches zero
the checksum of a frame is wrong
questions.exp: A choke packet is a feedback (closed-loop) signal from a congested router to the source asking it to slow down.

questions.q: Which device has multiple interfaces, works at the network layer, and keeps each interface in a separate broadcast domain?
questions.exp: Routers forward based on IP addresses and do not forward broadcasts, so each interface is its own broadcast domain.

questions.q: HTTP is a stateless protocol. What is the role of cookies?
options: To maintain state across separate HTTP requests
questions.exp: Cookies store small pieces of data at the client so that a server can recognise a user across stateless requests.

questions.q: A signal travels 2000 km through a medium at 2 × 10⁸ m/s. What is the propagation delay?
What is the broadcast address of the subnet to which the host 192.168.1.130/26 belongs?
questions.exp: /26 gives blocks of 64: 128–191. The host lies in 192.168.1.128/26 whose broadcast address is 192.168.1.191.

questions.q: Which protocol is used for exchanging routing information between different autonomous systems on the Internet?
questions.exp: BGP is the path-vector exterior gateway protocol used between autonomous systems.

questions.q: Admission control, in which the network refuses new connections when it is already heavily loaded, is an example of
options: flow control at the data link layer
questions.exp: Open-loop schemes prevent congestion by design or policy before it occurs; closed-loop schemes react to feedback (choke packets, backpressure, ECN).

questions.q: What is the range of well-known port numbers?
questions.exp: Well-known ports are 0–1023, registered ports 1024–49151 and dynamic/private ports 49152–65535.

questions.q: In the URL https://www.example.com:8080/index.html, what does 8080 represent?
questions.exp: The number after the colon following the host name is the TCP port of the web server.

questions.q: What is the subnet mask corresponding to a /26 prefix?
questions.exp: /26 means 26 network bits: 24 bits + 2 bits of the last octet = 11000000 = 192, so 255.255.255.192.

questions.q: Which statement about FTP is correct?
options: It uses a persistent control connection and a separate data connection for each transfer
It uses only one UDP connection for both commands and data
It encrypts the user name and password by default
It does not need a login in its default form
questions.exp: FTP has a control connection (port 21) kept for the session and data connections (port 20 in active mode) per transfer. TFTP is the one over UDP without login.
